questions.prompt: A student is answering an AQA-style practice question. Explain the energy transfers when a moving bicycle slows to a stop using its brakes. (4)
hints: Name energy stores before and after.
questions.solution:
The bicycle initially has energy in its kinetic store. [B1]
Friction does mechanical work on the brakes/wheels. [B1]
Energy is transferred mainly to thermal stores of the brakes, tyres and surroundings. [B1]
Total energy is conserved even though the useful kinetic energy decreases. [B1]

questions.prompt: A student is answering an AQA-style practice question. Explain two ways the rate of energy transfer from a house can be reduced. (4)
hints: Explain the physical mechanism for each.
questions.solution:
Loft insulation traps air and reduces conduction/convection through the roof. [B1]
Cavity wall insulation reduces conduction and convection through walls. [B1]
Double glazing traps a layer of gas and reduces conduction/convection through windows. [B1]
Thicker insulation generally reduces the rate of energy transfer, though cost and payback should also be considered. [B1]

questions.prompt: A student is answering an AQA-style practice question. Compare current and potential difference in a series circuit and a parallel circuit. (4)
hints: Recall the rules for series and parallel separately.
questions.solution:
In a series circuit the current is the same through all components. [B1]
In series, the supply potential difference is shared between components. [B1]
In parallel, the potential difference across each branch is the same as the supply. [B1]
In parallel, the total current equals the sum of currents in the branches. [B1]

hints: State the nature of each radiation.
questions.solution:
Alpha radiation consists of helium nuclei and is the least penetrating. [B1]
Beta radiation consists of fast electrons and has medium penetrating power. [B1]
Gamma radiation is electromagnetic radiation and is the most penetrating. [B1]

questions.solution:
It is impossible to predict exactly when a particular unstable nucleus will decay. [B1]
For a large sample the overall decay rate follows a predictable statistical pattern. [B1]
Half-life is the time for the number of undecayed nuclei or activity/count rate to fall to half its value. [B1]

questions.prompt: A student is answering an AQA-style practice question. Explain why the stopping distance of a car increases when the road is wet. (4)
questions.solution:
Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance. [B1]
Wet roads reduce friction between tyres and road. [B1]
The braking force is smaller, so deceleration is smaller. [B1]
The car travels further while braking, increasing braking and total stopping distance. [B1]

questions.prompt: A student is answering an AQA-style practice question. Describe the magnetic field around a bar magnet and explain how field lines show field strength. (4)
hints: State the direction outside the magnet.
questions.solution:
Outside the magnet, field lines go from the north pole to the south pole. [B1]
The field is strongest near the poles. [B1]
Closer field-line spacing represents a stronger magnetic field. [B1]
Field lines never cross because the field has one direction at each point. [B1]

questions.prompt: A student is answering an AQA-style practice question. Explain the motor effect on a current-carrying wire placed in a magnetic field. (4)
hints: Direction depends on both current and field.
questions.solution:
The magnetic field around the current interacts with the external magnetic field. [B1]
A force acts on the wire when current is not parallel to the field. [B1]
The force direction depends on current direction and magnetic field direction. [B1]
Increasing current or magnetic field strength increases the force. [B1]
